stem_book: If α is a non-real complex constant such that αz² + z + ᾱ = 0 has a real root, then (a) α + ᾱ = 1 (b) α + ᾱ = 0 (c) α + ᾱ = −1 (d) The absolute value of the real root is 1
reason: Added 'non-real' to the stem: for real α (e.g. α = 0.1) the equation has real roots yet none of the options hold; the intended answer assumes α ∉ R.
work: αx² + x + ᾱ = 0 and its conjugate ᾱx² + x + α = 0 ⇒ (α − ᾱ)(x² − 1) = 0 ⇒ x = ±1 ⇒ α + ᾱ = ∓1, |x| = 1
